title: Orchard MEX
statement:
ORCHARD MEX

An orchard row has N fruit trees numbered 1 to N. Tree i bears fruit of variety A_i (a non-negative integer). You are asked Q questions. Each question gives two integers L and R, and asks for the smallest non-negative integer variety (0, 1, 2, ...) that does NOT appear anywhere among trees L, L+1, ..., R.

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
The second line contains A_1 ... A_N.
Each of the next Q lines contains L and R.

Output
For each question print the smallest missing non-negative integer on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 200000
0 <= A_i <= N
1 <= L <= R <= N

0 2 1 0 3 1
1 3
2 5
1 6
5 6

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)

4
4
0

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Flooded Terraces
statement:
FLOODED TERRACES

Along a hillside stand N stone walls numbered 1 to N, where wall i has height H_i. You are asked Q independent questions. Each question specifies L and R: imagine that only walls L, L+1, ..., R exist (water spills freely off to the left of L and to the right of R). After heavy rain, water settles above each wall i (L <= i <= R) up to the height min(max_{L <= j <= i} H_j, max_{i <= j <= R} H_j). Find the total volume of trapped water summed over all i from L to R.

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
The second line contains H_1 ... H_N.
Each of the next Q lines contains L and R.

Output
For each question print the total trapped water volume on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 200000
1 <= H_i <= 10^9
1 <= L <= R <= N

title: Signal Relays
statement:
SIGNAL RELAYS

Across a desert plain are N signal relay towers. Tower i stands at integer coordinates (X_i, Y_i) and has transmission capacity W_i (multiple towers may share the same coordinates). You are asked Q sector queries. Each query specifies X_1, Y_1, X_2, Y_2 and asks for the sum of capacities W_i over all towers satisfying X_1 <= X_i <= X_2 and Y_1 <= Y_i <= Y_2.

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
Each of the next N lines contains X_i, Y_i, and W_i.
Each of the next Q lines contains X_1, Y_1, X_2, and Y_2.

Output
For each sector query print the total capacity on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 200000
1 <= X_i, Y_i, W_i <= 10^9
1 <= X_1 <= X_2 <= 10^9
1 <= Y_1 <= Y_2 <= 10^9

title: Toll Rebellion
statement:
TOLL REBELLION

A royal highway consists of N consecutive road segments numbered 1 to N, where segment i has length W_i kilometres. Initially there are no blockades on the highway. You process Q decrees in chronological order:
- 1 L R: a rebel guild erects a blockade covering segments L, L+1, ..., R.
- 2 L R: a previously erected blockade covering segments L, L+1, ..., R is lifted (it is guaranteed that at least one active blockade currently covers every segment from L to R; note that multiple blockades may overlap).

After each decree, print the total length in kilometres of segments that are currently covered by AT LEAST ONE active blockade.

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
The second line contains W_1 ... W_N.
Each of the next Q lines contains type, L, and R (type is 1 or 2).

Output
Print Q lines: after each decree, the total covered length in kilometres.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 200000
1 <= W_i <= 10^6
1 <= L <= R <= N

title: Imperial Beacons
statement:
IMPERIAL BEACONS

An empire consists of N fortress cities numbered 1 to N connected by N - 1 bidirectional roads forming a tree. City i houses W_i messengers, and road j connects U_j and V_j with length L_j.

If the imperial capital is placed at city c, every messenger in every city v must travel along the unique simple path from v to c, covering distance dist(v, c). Compute for every city c = 1, 2, ..., N the total distance travelled by all messengers: sum_{v=1..N} W_v * dist(v, c).

Input
The first line contains N.
The second line contains W_1 ... W_N.
Each of the next N - 1 lines contains U_j, V_j, and L_j.

Output
Print N lines: the i-th line should contain the total messenger distance if city i is chosen as capital.

Constraints
1 <= N <= 200000
1 <= W_i <= 10000
1 <= L_j <= 10000

title: Ancestral Archive
statement:
ANCESTRAL ARCHIVE

An academy of N scholars is organized as a rooted tree with scholar 1 as the grandmaster (root). Initially scholar i receives stipend A_i. Process Q events of two types:
- 1 U X: add X to the stipend of every scholar in the subtree of U (including U itself).
- 2 U V: report the sum of current stipends of all scholars on the unique simple path between U and V (inclusive).

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
The second line contains A_1 ... A_N.
Each of the next N - 1 lines contains two scholars connected by a direct mentorship link.
Each of the next Q lines describes an event in one of the two formats above. At least one event is of type 2.

Output
For each event of type 2, print the path sum on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 200000
-10^5 <= A_i, X <= 10^5
1 <= U, V <= N

FESTIVAL LANTERNS

A festival park has N plazas numbered 1 to N arranged as a rooted tree with plaza 1 at the entrance. Plaza i hangs a lantern of colour C_i.

For every plaza u (1 <= u <= N), count how many unordered pairs of distinct plazas {x, y} inside the subtree of u have the SAME lantern colour (C_x = C_y) AND have an EVEN number of walkways on the simple path between x and y.

The first line contains N.
The second line contains C_1 ... C_N.
Each of the next N - 1 lines contains two plazas connected by a walkway.

Output
Print N lines: the i-th line should contain the count of valid pairs inside the subtree of plaza i.

Constraints

1 <= C_i <= N

title: Emergency Depots

EMERGENCY DEPOTS

A kingdom has N cities numbered 1 to N connected by N - 1 bidirectional highways forming a tree, where highway j has length L_j.

You must evaluate Q emergency plans. Plan i specifies K_i distinct cities S_1, ..., S_{K_i}. Determine the minimum total length of highways that must be kept open so that all K_i specified cities are mutually reachable from one another (if K_i = 1, the answer is 0).

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
Each of the next N - 1 lines contains U_j, V_j, and L_j.
Each of the next Q lines begins with K_i followed by K_i distinct city numbers.
The sum of K_i over all Q plans does not exceed 300000.

Output
For each plan print the minimum total highway length on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 180000
1 <= L_j <= 10^6
1 <= K_i <= N
sum of K_i <= 300000

title: Guild Portals
statement:
GUILD PORTALS

A realm has N cities numbered 1 to N, M bidirectional roads, and G mage guilds. Road i connects U_i and V_i with travel time W_i. Guild j operates portals in K_j distinct cities; a traveller at any city belonging to guild j may teleport directly to ANY other city belonging to guild j in time C_j.

Find the minimum travel time from city 1 to every city 1, 2, ..., N (or -1 if a city cannot be reached).

Input
The first line contains N, M, and G.
Each of the next M lines contains U_i, V_i, and W_i.
Each of the next G lines begins with K_j and C_j, followed by the K_j city numbers in guild j.
The sum of K_j over all guilds does not exceed 250000.

Output
Print N space-separated integers on a single line: the minimum travel time from city 1 to cities 1, 2, ..., N (or -1 if unreachable).

Constraints
2 <= N <= 180000
0 <= M <= 180000
0 <= G <= 100000
2 <= K_j <= N, sum of K_j <= 250000
1 <= W_i, C_j <= 10^8

title: Sunken Causeways
statement:
SUNKEN CAUSEWAYS

An archipelago has N islands numbered 1 to N and M bidirectional stone causeways. Causeway i connects islands U_i and V_i at deck elevation H_i. When the sea tide rises to level T, every causeway with H_i <= T is submerged and impassable, while causeways with H_i > T remain open.

You are given Q tide forecasts. Each forecast specifies a starting island S and a tide level T: count how many islands (including S itself) can be reached from S using only open causeways.

Input
The first line contains N, M, and Q.
Each of the next M lines contains U_i, V_i, and H_i.
Each of the next Q lines contains S and T.

Output
For each forecast print the number of reachable islands on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= N <= 200000
0 <= M <= 200000
1 <= Q <= 200000
1 <= U_i, V_i, S <= N
1 <= H_i <= 10^9
0 <= T <= 10^9

CRITICAL AQUEDUCTS

A city water network consists of N reservoirs numbered 1 to N connected by M bidirectional pipes. The network is connected, and multiple parallel pipes may directly connect the same pair of reservoirs.

You are asked Q vulnerability queries. Each query specifies two reservoirs A and B: count how many single pipes have the property that removing ONLY that pipe would disconnect reservoir A from reservoir B.

The first line contains N, M, and Q.
Each of the next M lines contains two integers U_i and V_i (U_i != V_i), the endpoints of pipe i.
Each of the next Q lines contains A and B.

Output
For each query print the number of critical pipes between A and B on its own line.

Constraints

N - 1 <= M <= 220000
1 <= Q <= 180000
1 <= U_i, V_i, A, B <= N, U_i != V_i

title: Faction Truce
statement:
FACTION TRUCE

Along a frontier stand N forts numbered 1 to N. Over a campaign of T days (numbered 1 to T), each fort must be assigned every day to either the Dawn Watch or the Dusk Watch.

There are M rivalry pacts. Pact i specifies two forts U_i and V_i and a range of days [L_i, R_i]: on every day t with L_i <= t <= R_i, forts U_i and V_i refuse to serve on the same watch and must be assigned to OPPOSITE watches.

For each day t = 1, 2, ..., T, determine whether there exists a valid assignment of all N forts to the two watches satisfying all pacts active on day t.

Input
The first line contains N, M, and T.
Each of the next M lines contains U_i, V_i, L_i, and R_i.

Output
Print T lines: on line t print YES if a valid assignment exists on day t, or NO otherwise.

Constraints
2 <= N <= 150000
1 <= M, T <= 150000
1 <= U_i, V_i <= N, U_i != V_i
1 <= L_i <= R_i <= T

title: Convoy Escort
statement:
CONVOY ESCORT

A desert supply network has N outposts numbered 1 to N. Outpost i sends all departing convoys along a single one-way road directly to outpost P_i (possibly P_i = i), taking W_i hours.

You are given Q dispatch orders. Each order specifies a starting outpost S and a step count K: if a convoy starts at S and traverses exactly K roads one after another, determine which outpost it ends at AND the total hours spent travelling.

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
The second line contains P_1 ... P_N.
The third line contains W_1 ... W_N.
Each of the next Q lines contains S and K.

Output
For each dispatch order print two space-separated integers on its own line: the final outpost and the total travel time.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 200000
1 <= P_i, S <= N
1 <= W_i <= 10^6
1 <= K <= 10^15

title: Canal Locks
statement:
CANAL LOCKS

N freight barges arrive in a single file numbered 1 to N, where barge i has displacement W_i. You must divide the line of barges into exactly K non-empty contiguous batches to pass through a canal lock one batch at a time.

If a batch consists of barges L, L+1, ..., R, the water turbulence cost of locking that batch is (W_L + W_{L+1} + ... + W_R)^2. Find the minimum total turbulence cost summed across all K batches.

Input
The first line contains N and K.
The second line contains W_1 ... W_N.

Output
Print a single integer: the minimum possible total turbulence cost.

Constraints
1 <= K <= 20
K <= N <= 100000
1 <= W_i <= 10000

RUNE COMPATIBILITY

You are given Q ritual configurations. Each configuration specifies a master bitmask X: an apprentice i is compatible with X if every 1-bit in M_i is also a 1-bit in X (that is, (M_i & X) == M_i). For each configuration X, compute the sum of P_i over all compatible apprentices.

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
Each of the next N lines contains M_i and P_i.
Each of the next Q lines contains X.

Output
For each ritual configuration print the total compatible resonance on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 200000
0 <= M_i, X < 2^20 (i.e. at most 1048575)
1 <= P_i <= 10^6

MERCENARY WATCH

A fortress wall must be guarded continuously across N discrete hours numbered 1 to N. M mercenaries apply for work: mercenary i offers to guard every integer hour from L_i to R_i inclusive in exchange for wage W_i.

Select a subset of mercenaries so that every hour 1, 2, ..., N is guarded by at least one hired mercenary, minimizing the total wage paid (or report -1 if it is impossible to cover all N hours).

Input
The first line contains N and M.
Each of the next M lines contains L_i, R_i, and W_i.

Output
Print a single integer: the minimum total wage, or -1 if impossible.

Constraints
1 <= N, M <= 200000
1 <= L_i <= R_i <= N

VAULT RELICS

A royal vault holds N relics numbered 1 to N. Relic i has weight W_i and value V_i (at most one copy of each relic may be taken). The maximum possible satchel capacity is C.

You must answer Q contingency queries. Query j specifies a forbidden relic K_j and a satchel capacity B_j: if relic K_j may NOT be taken, what is the maximum total value of a subset of the remaining N - 1 relics whose total weight is at most B_j?

Each of the next N lines contains W_i and V_i.
Each of the next Q lines contains K_j and B_j.

1 <= C <= 2000
1 <= Q <= 120000

1 <= K_j <= N

TWIN INSCRIPTIONS

Starting with vitality 0 and walking from vial 1 to vial k, the alchemist may choose to drink or skip each vial in order, subject to the rule that vitality must NEVER drop below 0 at any moment.

ORE ASSAY

title: Artisan Alloys

ARTISAN ALLOYS

Within a single segment [L, R], an inversion is a pair of indices (i, j) with L <= i < j <= R and A_i > A_j.

Find the minimum possible value of M such that the array can be partitioned into at most K contiguous segments where EVERY segment contains at most M internal inversions.

d_1 <= d_2 <= ... <= d_{N*(N-1)/2}.

title: Domino Cascade

DOMINO CASCADE

N dominoes stand along a number line at strictly increasing integer coordinates X_1 < X_2 < ... < X_N. Domino i has positive height H_i.

For EACH starting domino i = 1, 2, ..., N (considered independently, starting with all dominoes upright), compute how many dominoes in total end up knocked over (including domino i itself).

Hydraulic flow requires that for every consecutive pair of piers (i - 1, i) with 2 <= i <= N, the elevation step satisfies:
L_i <= B_i - B_{i-1} <= R_i.

HARBOR BEACONS

An archipelago kingdom has N coastal harbors numbered 1 to N connected by N - 1 bidirectional sea lanes forming a tree, with the royal capital at harbor 1. Sea lane i has length W_i kilometers.

Each harbor u (for 2 <= u <= N) has a courier boat that requires S_u minutes of launch preparation and then travels toward the capital at a pace of P_u minutes per kilometer.

You may transfer as many times as you wish.
